title: One Task, One Timer.
body:
Many years ago, when I was studying and writing assignments, I followed the idea of focusing on one task at a time. I expanded this approach by adding a timer to each task, and I found it extremely helpful.

After completing my degree, I gradually drifted away from this method.

More recently, as my life circumstances have changed, I’ve found it harder to concentrate. So I’ve returned to the principle of focusing on a single activity at a time—no multitasking. I’ve also found that this works best when the activity is planned for a limited, defined period. This allows for regular breaks, which helps prevent mental fatigue and overload, and it adds a helpful sense of structure.

You can extend these timed periods if you wish, as long as you include breaks. I use this app to manage that.

If you want to maximise your results and be as productive as possible, I recommend using the Pomodoro timer and technique alongside your daily plan. It helps maintain structure and keeps you focused on each task.

It will improve the quality of your life.

title: Does what it says on the tin
body:
This app provides a full-screen timer, nicely laid out, showing numerical countdown as well as a simulated rotary timer. The app is extremely focussed on helping you use the Pomodoro Technique. Go read up about it on Wikipedia if you haven't heard of this popular productivity tool.

The timer has three "phases": the work, rest and long-break phases. The default configuration is four "pomodoros" of 25 minutes broken by a 5 minute rest, with a 25 minute long break at the end. You can manually adjust the timers, though setting default durations for each period is only possible in the paid app.

The ticking sound is a nice reminder that you are supposed to be focussed on one task. Some people won't like it, you can turn it off in the paid version of the app.

The app also includes daily goals of 12 pomodoros. Achievement of this goal is reported through charts.

My only quibble with this app was the end of period alerts which are once-off chimes. They are easy to miss when listening to music. You do get banner notifications though.

For many people, using the Clock app on your iPad or iPhone will work just as well, though I find this app is more charming than Apple's timer app. The charm keeps me using this Pomodoro timer though!

title: The app is almost awesome. It just has one problem.
body:
Focus Keeper Pro is the best pomodoro app in Apple Store. But it has only one problem: the scroll on the main screen. First, let’s see the pros. Then, I’ll explain the cons.

The pros are: 
- The interface is simple and beautiful. 
- It gives me the report of the last 14 days (in hours).
- The times are adjustable.
- It doesn’t have bugs when it counts my pomodoros of the day (as others do). 

The only con:

- It uses scroll to adjust the time.

Sometimes I touch the screen by mistake just after starting the pomodoro. As a result, de scroll rolls and it doesn’t play the time because that app thinks I am setting a new time. Thus, I start studying without tracking my time while I think I am tracking it. That is the only problem with Focus Keeper.

The scroll isn’t much helpful to me. The way other apps set time, like Be Focused and Tide, prevent me from not tracking my time because there is no scroll to touch by mistake.

title: Issues with Latest Update
body: I have been using this app for a long time and have been very happy with it. I even paid for the full version. However, after the latest update, it has suffered from significant issues, the main one being background running. Simply put, the break timer will no longer start running unless the app is open and your screen is unlocked. I used to be able to lock my screen and the break/focus timers would run automatically. Now, if I lock my screen, the break timer will not start, or will start late and throw off the whole focus/break cycle. Changing the settings has not helped, and support has not adresses the issue despite my many follow ups. Now, I have to leave the screen on and the app open if I want it to work, which affects my screen time and battery. It is unfortunate that such a useful app os suffering from such an unnecessary issue. Hopefully it gets fixed soon.

title: Absolutely Awesome! Love it!
body:

   I have been feverishly going through many pomodoro and other timer apps over the past few days and have spent way too much money in order to upgrade some. This is by far the easiest, most flexible, most appealing and pleasing to the eye and ear one I’ve found. 
   Only three requests; 1. a one minute warning alert as you come to the end of each segment of time. 2. something to tell me how long the total length of my current session was have and what’s up next (eg 2 minute short break) and, most importantly,  3. the app work in tandem with my Apple Watch. Please, please, PLEASE!!!
   Thank you for your hard, exceptional work!

title: Nice app but vibration is too short
body:
The app is really nice but I would line to point out 2 features that would be really nice: -being able to choose a custom vibration pattern. currently, the vibration when the phone is silenced is too short for me. I often do not notice the break alerts and I can‘t change the vibration pattern to be longer (I can change the sound but not how long the vibration is) -it would be really nice to have timers without the pomodoro features. that way, you could have multiple timers tracking for example the intake of prescription drugs or time spent in the gym or running, without scheduling breaks or having to know how long it will take.

Also I think it is absolutely crucial to have a widget for the to-do list and then a separate one for the currently selected pomodoro. Otherwise using this app as your personal to do app becomes much too annoying !

Warum muss eine Timer-App auch gleich Kalender und To-Do-Liste sein? Statt einfach meine Fokus-Zeiten und Zahl der absolvierten Sessions einsehen zu können, sind die Statistiken jetzt nach Aufgaben oder Tags sortiert. Mir wird zu meinem neuen „Streak“ gratuliert, und ich kann Auszeichnungen sammeln. Was ist aus den guten alten Apps geworden, die einfach nur ihren Zweck erfüllt haben?

—

Alte Rezension:

Schlicht und gut

Tut, was es soll - ohne ablenkenden Schnickschnack. Als jemand, der Daten und Grafiken liebt, freut und motiviert mich die Übersicht über die beendeten Fokuszeiten besonders.

title: 4.75 Sterne...
body:
Diese App ist mein Retter in der Not! Wirklich genial und auch in der Pro-Version preislich gesehen unschlagbar zu anderen Apps.

Trotzdem habe ich ein paar Verbesserungsvorschläge, welche Sie auf ein volles 5 Sterne Niveau anheben würde:

Synchronisation: iCloud Synchronisiert nicht - das sollte verbessert werden, sodass ich die App mal am iPhone und mal am iPad bedienen kann.
Zudem wäre es genial die App auch auf dem Mac zu haben.

Focus Reminder: diesen sollte man wenigstens Viertelstündlich einstellen können, nicht nur stündlich.

Widget: hier wäre eine Pause/Play Funktion super, ohne das sich dabei die App öffnet.

Sperrbildschirm: Am genialsten wäre es, wenn die Restzeit des aktuellen Timers im Sperrbildschirm angezeigt würde, ähnlich wie beim Apple Timer... dann müsste man nicht ins Widget rüber gehen, um zu sehen wie lange man noch Pause/Lernzeit im aktuellen Block hat.

Aber trotz meiner Vorschläge - großes Kompliment an die Entwickler! Es hilft wirklich dabei fokusierter zu lernen ;)

jetzr höre ich beim lernen 25 min lang das geräusch von Wellen und bin dadurch total fokussiert. 5min pause sind einfach viel zu kurz um irgendwas sinnvolles zu machen und das ist gut so! so entspannt man tatsächlich in diesen 5min und lässt sich nicht ablenken oder macht tausend andere sachen. 
Dadurch das nach vier durchgängen eine große pause folgt und man ein tagesziel hat, liegt das ende immer irgendwo im blickfeld und es fühlt sich nicht so endlos an wie einfaches stundenlanges lernen. 
Ich habe es auch so schön mit dem pomodoro system probier und es lief nur mäßig daher war ich mir nicht sicher wie viel diese App mir bringt aber sie ist wirklich toll! Dadurch das die App offen ist ist mein handy auch keine Ablenkung beim lernen mehr und es fällt mir leichter mich zu konzentrieren. 
Im Ernst ich hätte das nicht erwartet aber ich habe noch nie so konzentriert gelernt wie mit dieser App 😅

title: Needs more customised templates
body:
Great app for basic Pomodoro focus sessions, but I’d love to see more customisation. It would be fantastic if users could create and save different focus templates for specific tasks. For example, a work template with a professional background and office ambience, a study template with library sounds, and a learning template with café noise. Ideally, each template would save its own timer length, background, ambient sounds, and alarm settings so everything could be launched with a single tap instead of having to change settings every time. The app is simple and effective, but adding custom focus environments would take it to the next level.

This has put me off slightly

title: Genuinely amazing app. Well worth the money
body: There is a free version which is also easy to use and very helpful, but I have the paid version and I can honestly say this is one of the few apps nowadays that’s actually worth the money. Easy to use, customisable, so many different features that all help you keep on track, including one (optional) that prevents you from using other apps during a focus session. Great for people who get distracted or just need to get long tasks done regularly and don’t want to burn out. You can customise the length of breaks and focus sessions too, which is great for days you need a little more time between sessions to keep going. It also not has a feature where you can plan your day (and integrate your existing calendar) and have a visual of what your schedule looks like. Just so many great features. Highly recommend!

title: I’m lost without it.
body:
I’m someone dyslexia and recently been diagnosed with ADHD. I’m also a mature student at university studying psychology. Having ADHD has been a serious issue for me to deal with. The lack of focus and being unable to concentrate until a looming deadline approaches and then my super-power hyper-focus kicks in. However, using this app is seriously becoming a game changer for me. Being able to study in sort blocks of 25 mins, then a 5 minute rest, really does work. But what I love the most is the ticking clock! It’s a nice touch. Just the sound in the background seems to calm my mind, helps me keep less distracted by external stimuli. 
I can’t rate this app highly enough. It’s getting me through my degree ☺️

title: Flexible timer settings, but lacking stats
body:
By comparison to all the other pomodoro apps on the store, this is the only one that suited my needs. So why did I rate 2 stars? Let me explain. 

First of all, I’m reviewing the pro version of the app (am I the only one cringing at the thought of a timer being marketed as “professional”?). Once you pass the paywall you can adjust the lengths of you work and short/long breaks. That seems like it should be the minimum bar for a timer app, but apparently it’s a premium feature. The devs are within their rights to charge for it I suppose because no free pomodoro app on the store seems to allow easy manual time setting... Some even charge a subscription fee. So that’s where this app wins the stars - one for allowing me to set manual timers when no others will, and a second for the other more inconsequential customisation options (timer colours, timer chimes).

But I think the app is lacking when it comes to stats. You can see your average working time over 30 days or 14 days, but nothing more. It’d be better if the devs would let us enter our own time periods to see averages, because otherwise stats sections is almost pointless for the first two weeks, aside from checking your daily work time. It would be better still if the amount of time spent working each day could be represented more clearly on the focus page, rather than the stats page. At the mount you get to see how many “rounds” you’ve done. This means how many times you’ve set a timer and worked through it. But if you work through one 25min timer and then a 50min timer, that is still only represented as 2 rounds. It would be nice to have the option to change the metric from rounds to minutes on the focus screen.

All-in-all, it’s fine. It’s worth the £2 spend, only because no other apps give you the same flexibility for cheaper. But let’s face it - setting a custom timer should be the real minimum bar for a timer app. And useful features like stats should have been developed ahead of quality of life features like a chime that meows like a cat.

title: C’è un problema con lo speaker
body:
Ottima applicazione: funziona alla perfezione, è semplice ed essenziale nella grafica ed è una delle poche che sincronizza i dati e li rende disponibili anche su iPad nel caso si vogliano poi rivedere da lì le sessioni di studio fatte.

Unico problema: anche disattivando il suono impostando “none” in ogni sua parte e mettendo anche il volume a zero, se si avvicina l’orecchio allo speaker mentre scorre il timer, si sente un certo brusio che sparisce immediatamente quando si mette in pausa il timer, lo speaker è quindi comunque acceso!
Sarebbe meglio che lo speaker fosse proprio SPENTO mentre scorre il timer quando si toglie il suono e si mette il volume a zero, così da non sprecare batteria inutilmente! 
Specifico che è solo una questione di batteria, se non avvicino l’orecchio non sento nulla perché, il brusio è praticamente impercettibile.
Tuttavia in 4h di utilizzo in background ha consumato il 12% della batteria, Forest (app che stava facendo la stessa cosa, ossia contare il tempo in background) ne ha consumato il 2% nelle stesse 4h. 
Senza il problema dello speaker attivo mentre scorre il timer (anche avendo messo il volume del suono della sessione a zero e il suono come “none”) avrei messo 5 stelle.

5 stelle appena sarà corretto e avvicinando l’orecchio non sentirò più il brusio dello speaker attivo!

title: Ironically, this developer lost focus
body:
This used to be a fairly decent app, but after many years of use of this app, and the old app from this developer, I will now stop using this app. It is just getting worse and worse with every update, while issues are not being fixed.

My biggest gripes :
- The UI is more and more getting bloated with new features that are not needed by me, but that are pushed to the front in an effort to monetise the app.
- Meanwhile a feature that is vital for the pomodoro technique is moved to a sub-menu, when it used to be front and center.
- The app now frequently asks for feedback, just when I start a focus timer. Rarely the developers response to the feedback. What an extremely weird moment to ask for feedback, when the user just starts a focus session.
-  When the app is run in the background the app shows live activity information about the timer in the top of the screen, and on the lock screen, showing information about the timer. This is a big plus compared to similar focus apps. However, it gives outdated information once a focus session has ended and a new one (or a break) has been started automatically. I've reported this multiple times, but the app developer seems unable to fix this, so I have to get used to reading incorrect information.
- The same applies to the widget that can be added to the home screen. It shows information about the number of focus rounds I did, but most of the time it shows outdated information, and I need to manually open the app to update the information. It defeats the purpose of a widget. Instead of fixing this the developers have 'fixed' this by now sometimes just showing a refresh button that opens the app. How other apps are able to show updated information in their widgets and this app seemingly not is beyond me.
- While the app seems to be designed to be able to run in the background, if I actually do that the app classifies this as me being distracted during a focus session, and bugs me with a popup about it, hoping to sell the Focus Shield feature I don't need. The developers should not pretent to know if me using another app while in a focus session is related to the focus session or me actually being distracted. But they do, just to use it in order to try to sell.
- When the app is run it the background it not always sounds an alarm when the timer has ended, while this is the most important feature of any focus timer app. It happens rarely, but it does happen.
- I wanted to switch back to the old free version, but the developer removed that version from the store.

”I can stay productive for hours with this app, it’s so simple I mean it’s just a timer, but still it makes such a difference to me, I love it!! It’s so easy to use, and it helps me remembering to take frequent breaks during study hours” - me a month ago on App Store (I gave 5 stars)

After I gave this feedback all the free advantages with noice notifications from the app was taken away? So all the noice features which helped me to stay focused and in my zone suddenly disappeared which meant I had to constantly check on the timer to know when to take a break and now I can’t use this app to study like I did before. I’m very disappointed because this app really helped me so much before due to my ADHD :( felt like a betrayal after my 5-star feedback

title: How long are we gonna put up with this?
body:
First off, the pricing model is totally predatory. The only free trial is if you agree to be charged a whole year’s membership fee after the seven-day trial period.  There’s no free trial if you opt for just monthly payments. I wonder why that would be?  Also, how long are we going to tolerate apps asking you a bunch of irrelevant questions prior to even being able to test the app?  Can I please just test your service without feeling like I’m being herded?   

When I finally got to the app, I realized it was overly complicated and could not really do what I wanted it to do, which was track the amount of time I spend in specific habits by using timers for those activities.  Overall, I feel like I was charged $13 so that I could make the 30 second assessment that this app was not for me. This could have been avoided with a free trial.

title: Issue Summary
body:
Issue Summary:
I noticed a problem in how Focus Keeper calculates focus time during a Pomodoro cycle.
Today, I completed the first session normally. In the second session, I had 7 minutes left but had to stop and leave the app from morning until late at night. When I came back at night, I finished the remaining 7 minutes, then completed sessions 3 and 4.
My real focus time for the day was 100 minutes.
However, the Achievements page counted the long break (from morning to night) as if it were focus time, and showed more than 10 hours of focus.
Expected behavior: The app should count only the actual minutes spent focusing, even if a session is paused for many hours.
Actual behavior: When a session is paused for a long time, the app adds the entire real-world gap to the focus total, which makes the daily focus time incorrect.
Please fix this issue so the focus time reflects actual work time only.

title: Works for me! Even with ADHD.
body:
I use this for the pomodoro all the time. I began to use the app as an alternative to my traditional tomato timer. I fought it at first because I still prefer the mechanical tick of the tomato timer. I find the tick keeps me track when I drift. However the convenience of having it on my phone means I can listen to music, audiobooks, or YouTube and I know that I will always hear the ding. I like that it tracks my daily streak so I can see how consistent I am. I like that it logs your sessions and how long you worked that day. This lets me get an idea of how much focus work I can do in a day. I like how you can change the timer settings so you can change what works for me and my situation. 

All in all, it does what I needed (and then some) which is having a timer that I can carry with me no matter the task.

title: Loved this app until the latest update.
body: Prior to the latest update I absolutely loved the app. I was a free user, and even then it did exactly what I wanted it to: set pomodoro seshes, track my time among different tasks—it was perfect. The option to block apps was there (though I personally never used it). Now, the app forces app blockage, and the only way to really get rid of it is to manually block screen time access in settings, which we shouldn’t have to do in the first place. We shouldn’t have to PAY to turn off a feature that we were previously able to toggle ourselves. I agree with many recent reviews in that this 100% feels like a money grabbing update. Most of all, I dislike the inability to pause automatically timers whenever a focus or break session is done. Instead, it automatically goes into the next break or focus session. Though for some they prefer this feature, me personally it makes me lose track of what focus session I’m on. A pause  allows me to better keep track of it, and the fact that this is no longer a feature is driving me away from this app.

title: Elegance and functionality declining with every new update
body: This was a 5 star app and now it’s a 2 or 3 star. The original reason I chose this app many years ago is because it had the simplest, elegant design while also offering key features like easy customization of the short and long break timing, number of sessions, notifications, ability to pause and restart. Then came the updates and gamification, trying to be something that it never will be: a task management app? From someone with lifelong ADHD, it’s disappointing that you’re jumping on the more is better bandwagon. More is more confusing and clunky and honestly very cheesy if not implemented well. I’m looking for a sleek tool for the toolbox not a new toolbox. Many new updates in this app interrupts core functionality and usability and often causes more distraction and less focus. Have you tested the UX of this app thoroughly? Have user groups weighed in? I just begrudgingly opened for the first time in a while and now I can’t find any way to set the number of sessions. Months ago wasn’t much better—while you still could adjust the break options, there were two different ways to do it (global and task specific) and neither worked well. I usually had to restart for the timer to adjust. I have zero issue paying a reasonable fee for a good app. But that’s only if it’s going to thoughtful design. I wish it would stop trying to be the gimmicky and clunky gamification apps. There is a way to maintain features without them getting in the way of ppl who don’t want them. I am so sad to say I’m finally going to cancel after years of paying membership.

title: Useful, but recent updates make it worse
body:
I’ve used and appreciated this app for over a year and it has really made a difference. However, I became very used to its system of numbering focus sessions. I track how many I’ve done on a white board, and the numbering system on the app allowed me to double check that I was in the right place with it. 

In an update maybe a month ago, they changed how these numbers worked, so that they no longer reset after two tomatoes, with no setting option to keep it with the old numbering. This wasn’t the end of the world, as I could just reset it myself every two hours. However, the most recent update removes the numbers completely, and I can find no way to get them back. It replaces them with little visual tomatoes instead, which I can’t tell if they indicate halves at all or not. Either way, I and others would really appreciate a toggleable option to use the legacy numbering system. 

I know this is a small thing, but I think it’s the kind of thing that can have a big impact on specifically the groups of people who find this app most useful. I hope this is seen and I want to add that I’m very appreciative the app has as much functionality as it does even on the free tier!!

title: Subscription Model
body: Paid for the app some time ago as a one time purchase. The recent update switched to a subscription model. I am more than willing to pay for large updates (big releases of apps), but a subscription for this sort of application is not the right direction. I understand the developers need to make money for the updates they make, but a subscription model is not the way to go if there are no substantial reoccurring costs beyond the time cost of development. If huge improvements are made and new features are added, I’d rather make another one time purchase. If instead, you had released a v2 separately as a one time purchase (even a much steeper price would have been ok), I would have been more than happy to have bought the new app. I want to make it very clear that subscriptions for apps that run almost entirely locally is not a trend I’m willing to get behind. I don’t blame the developer(s), since this is a common trend, but I also want to make clear to them the loss of a potential sale and the reason why.

title: Terrible Apple Watch support
body:
Using the app on a phone? Great! Using it on the Watch? Not great. 

Although this is indeed fully-featured Pomodoro software with great customizability and strong attention to detail in control granularity, I cannot justify the premium cost required to unlock most features when the app’s Apple Watch support is this bare-bones. Since I boost my productivity by making my iPhone inaccessible during work hours, I rely on Apple Watch apps and tools. 

The Focus Keeper Watch app has no watchface complication support, no Smart Stack widget, and works by tethering and mirroring the phone app’s timer. If the connection to the phone is interrupted, the timer stutters and stalls. I will be subscribing to a competitor who has an actual Watch app that runs on the Watch itself.

title: How can that happen?!
body:
Hi, first I will apologize to rate it with 1 star, but one I explain the reason, you may will agree you give me no other choice.

I just purchased the app to help me in focusing on my work and… in the very first time I’m using it, during the first 25 minutes… the app send me a pup-up to write a review, getting my focus away from my work.

So, the 1 single star is for two reasons. First of all is the pup-up coming on my screen during the focusing time, and second is asking me to rate the app 20 minutes after I have purchased it. 

I’m sorry folks, but you all need to looking at a better way to approach your customers to rate your app.

Anyway, I promise I will continue to be fair with my reviews and if this app proves to be a great tool, I will score a 5 stars with fare comments, but if more pup-up keep coming, I will just cancel my 7 days free trial. 

Thanks and I hope this comments will help you guys to improve and get more customers.

Best regards,
PG

title: Deserving of 5 stars but missing 2 features
body:
So for starters, I love this app. It’s relatively simple, the interface is great. I love that it gives you data about your studying and where the time went. I pay for the premium version. Here’s my complaints, or suggestions.

1) Dev’s can you please make it so that I can manually add time?! I hate when I study for 10 minutes and then realize I forgot my timer. My total hours studied is never accurate because of this.

2) Allow multiple graphs which you can assign task to specific graphs. For example I would love to use this as a study timer for school as well as guitar. It shows me the time, and allows me to see where it was all spent. It’s perfect for both my hobby and school. It’d be wonderful if I could have two seperate graphs one for guitar and one for school.

3) *not really bothered by this but still… I’d love it if you guys allowed tags for sessions and sorting by them. For example if I look back on Wednesday I can see the red tag meaning that was a day I was sleep deprived, and I studied x on that day. Now it makes a little more sense why for some reason I just don’t remember that content as well.

I’d love to hear your thoughts about this if you see it dev’s.

title: Extreme privacy data collection
body: I downloaded this and ditched it after going to their link and reading their privacy policies. They are quite extreme, and be skeptical if the developer replies and makes it sound like you can opt out of them. Their own site says in clear terms that opting out makes the app basically nonfunctional. I’ve used many apps, including having tried several Pomodoro apps, and this is one of the worst as far as your privacy rights. Your personal data should not be for sale or shared with entities like Facebook, Google, and others for advertising or ANY purposes. You’re already paying a subscription fee. There are other issues like their statement that they can retain your data as long as needed, but they don’t tell you what that period is after you delete your app. Flimsy wording like this is a sign of a developer who only has his own interests in mind, and I refuse to patronize developers who gather and share my personal data to this extent. Privacy matters. Regardless of any possible future response by the developer to downplay these issues I’ve mentioned, I encourage you to click the link and read their privacy policy for yourself.

title: Paid upgrade not worth it
body:
PROS:

Great timer to lead us ADHD-ers into getting at least a little bit of something (or anything at all) completed. Paid version: keep track of additional tasks and customize timer intervals.

CONS:

Paid version still limited to (I think) 8 tasks. Can't edit timers after accidentally running them. Bug at midnight sometimes loses the session time. 

DEVS:

1.) Fix the midnight bug; it seems that if I left my timer on past midnight, when the session finished that time disappeared completely from the task before midnight and the task after midnight remained zero. 2.) I want to be able to rearrange my stack of tasks, which can't be done without deleting the task and its history. Please add a "press-hold" action on task list to rearrange/edit my individual task timers. 3.) Add ability to edit timers that were accidentally left on, including applying timer to a different task that I started doing and forgot to switch task timers. 4.) Make timer accessible from Lock Screen.

i never write reviews but had to for this app. 
It worked great for 2 days. Then stopped working like other people said. I thought it may just be me so I deleted the app and reinstalled. Nope. Still doesn't work. You press set timer and it starts counting down and come back and find out it is still stuck at the time you set it. What a waste. Do not download this timer. Find one that is reliable.
author: Morganooche

title: App is unusable without a subscription
body:
I paid for this app years ago and it was wonderful. I've recommended it to countless friends and family. However, after not updating for a while, I discovered I have to now pay a subscription to simply change settings.

I have already paid for this app. I do not want any of the advanced functionality. I simply want a single timer with a break and the ability to change their lengths.

This app used to provide that functionality, which, again, I had paid for. It has since been taken away and replaced with a paywall.

I'm done with Focus Keeper.
author: snevine

title: Previously was amazing, now....not really.
body: I used to use this app two years ago and it was fantastic. But now, it is quite buggy and no longer usable, imo. I will have to find another app, now.
author: Cheshirecatluv

title: Loved the app until the recent update
body:
Temp one star review

Now the timer only runs if you have the app open, and opening the app interrupts audio from phone. Please return to pre-update functionality!
author: Dvcdq

title: Good but could be better.
body: I like the app and the 25 minute study sessions are very helpful. The only thing that would improve the app would be to add statistics for the skills. I’d like to know how much time I have spent in total in the reading skill or the other skills. It would also be nice to see a chart showing how much time was spent over time.
author: eidhbofjsbidhsvddih

title: Pretty buggy
body: The app does not save changes made in settings sometimes. It’s really a shame because the app has all the features I need…if they’d work consistently!
author: Shaloha91

title: Free one not worth it
body: It has nothing beyond what you can get from the net. Pointless.
author: Alisaspeaks

title: Worked for one day
body: Then like all BRILLIANT updates, it made the app useless. I do work on this device sometimes and the app would run in the background, perfectly timing and adding the Pomodoro structure. It’s very easy to use compared to other apps. Now this app has an update where it will only run when you are actively on an app.. that just has a timer. I can just as easily manage timers from my phone so goodbye, thanks for one day of use!
author: RC1📛

title: Wow!
body: As someone who struggles with stay focused and on task, this app has been a game changer. After reading Deep Work by Cal Newport, I need something to keep me focused without distraction and this has done the trick. My only issue is that sometimes when I go to start the timer, it doesn’t start and I have to end the timer for it to work. If you guys can fix that, it’s perfect for my needs!
author: martbenj4

title: Timer doesn’t work since updates
body: This app used to be great, but since they’ve added all kinds of new features, the timer became really buggy. It won’t start when I hit the button, it starts but then loses its time, etc. i don’t need another planner/organizer app that does it all, I just need a pomodoro timer and I need it work
author: Captaineothan

title: Bizarre Default Settings
body: Why would anyone think that an app that is meant to enhance productivity should have a loud ticking sound on by default? Why would the timer not work without a task being selected? Why doesn’t the app start on the tab for the feature you’re actually there to use?
author: go dunk

title: Buggy and unreliable
body: This app has become completely buggy and unreliable in the last update or two. Going to delete it and find something else.
author: User 45328

title: Stay Away!
body:
I typically don’t write reviews, but this app is deeply frustrating. As one can see from the recent reviews, not only did their recent update add a paywall for a pro version, despite being a long term user who earlier payed, the updates also effectively break the app. At the moment, it’s difficult to even get the clock started, despite pressing the start button. Finally, after seeing a review on here mentioning a Baby Story Pics Editor being installed on iCloud, I also checked my iCloud and found the app there too. Really creepy. 

It’s really sad that the new changes ruined the app. I loved this app and it helped me focus on, and definitely when the pandemic hit. I hope they change their approach sometime. Until then, I will be moving on.
author: Montagnard1793

title: Keeps crashing, even after update
body:
For a while now, the application has been crashing repeatedly.  I just upgraded to the new version and the problem persists.  This makes the application completely unusable.

Please fix this!
author: Jaz--

title: Cool app but secretly installed other app data
body:
I haven’t written a review in years so please read. 

This is a great app but the issue is that they install Baby Story Pics Editor data on your iCloud storage. Don’t believe me? Go check for yourself I was completely unaware of this and I have deleted the app as a result. Until this is removed I will not download the app.
author: Michael 1098

title: Too many unnecessary features
body:
You ruined a great app by requiring customers to use unnecessary feature. I need:

Short timer
Long timer 
Tick tick tick
The ability to reset the day

Fix this bloated monstrosity by allowing customers to turn useless features off.
author: Phranqburke

title: No longer capable of turning sideways?
body: I’ve had this app for years and I just updated and it no longer rotates to landscape view. Is anyone else having this issue? Am I missing something?
author: hdogksbcjf

title: Great Tool for Those with ADHD
body: I've been diagnosed with ADHD for about 10 years now, and as such, I've been through quite a few apps when trying to figure out a method of studying. I know this isn't the only place to access a pomodoro timer but it is definitely my favorite. The app is super intuitive to use (just hit a button to start and you're good to go). Even the price for pro is something I'd consider paying if you find it worth it. Normally, I scoff when I see the price of the "premium" version of an app, when in reality it's just a paywall to ensure I have to pay money to get the true functionality of the app, but Focus Keeper is super affordable and actually doesn't limit much by having pro features. All you really need the app for is the timer, and it's got that covered. The only thing you miss out on by not going pro is having a breakdown of your stats and editing the length of timers.
author: laypersonn

title: Best study app tool ever
body: I have a really hard time keeping track of time in studying for anything or keeping on track this app has been absolutely saver for school it has had me on time for all my deadlines it has kept me really really good grades. I love this app and I will definitely recommend it if you get sidetracked easily
author: hhhhhhussnid

title: Only 1 minor issue
body: The only problem I have is that I can’t use other apps while my timer is going. I recognize the benefits of this but I use the timer to Keto track of how much time I spend on something so it’s a bit frustrating. Maybe this could be something to toggle on and off in settings?
author: Danielle_Layne

title: Good Feature Became Subscription Only
body: This app has been a solid work companion for two years. I would listen to a custom concentration song while I worked. That would have made this a 5 star app. But recently they moved that feature into the subscription only feature. I have stopped using it ever since.
author: Love Doc-yet

title: Great App but stops clock when leaving app
body:
I really like this app and has really helped me focus in a WFH environment.

Only reason this isn’t 5 stars is if your phone locks or you leave the app it stops the clock. Totally fine if it’s been a few seconds, but it becomes a problem if you forget to go back. Not to mention this drains the battery being on all the time.
author: rythebadger

title: Garbage
body: Wants a monthly subscription to unlock features. Awful
author: Echo Location

title: Used to be great
body: I used to love this app, but with the recent update the timer no longer runs in the background. If I switch over to Spotify to put on some chill focus music the timer pauses, and when I go back to the timer it pauses my music. So disappointing!
author: CET520

title: Removed basic features to push subscriptions
body: What's the point of the free version if you can no longer change the timer? You're stuck with 25 minute sessions unless you pay for the pro upgrade. Ridiculous.
author: NXCIX

title: THEY STOLE MY MONEY. DO NOT BUY!!!
body: I already paid for this app to get access to the basic functionalities you would expect from an app like this. Got a new phone, downloaded the app on it. And now I need to subscribe to get basic functionalities for a timer app THAT I ALREADY PAID FOR! Hitting “restore purchase” doesn’t work. Please REFUND ME THE MONEY I PAID. And don’t tell me to reach out via email. This is ridiculous. This app is not worth a subscription fee in general. It’s definitely not worth a subscription fee to gain features I already had after I paid a single price! I see others have the same problem. Please buy a different app.
author: axyz_4

title: Used for 5 years, no longer reccomend
body: I’ve used this app regularly since 2017 and have told many, many people to download it. Through that time it has consistently improved and added more features until now- the addition of a subscription model. I even paid for the “pro version “ when it came out because I simply wanted to support the creators. However I don’t respect that people who have used the app for so long haven’t been grandfathered in- at least for the first year. I hate that everything is becoming subscription based and creators are all about the micro transactions. I’m happy to pay a one- off fee for a great product but the cost really adds up, and what are you really getting for it? Very disappointed.
author: Sleapy head

title: What a racket
body: Loved the app, bought the paid version. Now that they've switched to a subscription model, I can no longer use the extra features that I paid for.
author: jakes apple store nickname

title: New Update Not Clear Or Fair
body: I had pro for the previous version and now I’m being asked to pay to upgrade to pro again, and the option to change colors of the screens are different. Red is not a focus incentive for everyone. I’m not sure what happened, but please change the app back, thank you.
author: SiSi The Lyricist

body: Suddenly updated to a pro version and all my last month’s task logs/hours cannot be accessed anymore. At least give users a heads-up!
author: mjsoup

title: They’ve not fixed the bug yet…
body: Not sure why I paid for a year’s subscription starting in august and now all my data has cleared and it’s telling me to upgrade for my focus stats, but I’ve already paid for the upgrade. It’s been like this for a few weeks, so don’t waste your money on it. The app isn’t set up as well as other focus apps anyway, so it’s not worth the money.
author: StudyToEsq

title: Love but Mad!
body: I was using this app frequently to help me stay on-task during the summer and fall months and I’ve loved using it every time. However, I purchased the 1 year Pro subscription on July 28, 2021. It’s not due to expire until July 29, 2022. But when I went into it today for the first time in a few weeks, I’m not being allowed to access my Pro perks. A pop-up screen keeps telling me to purchase the Pro subscription instead. I ALREADY DID AND ITS SUPPOSED TO STILL BE ACTIVE!!! I want access to what I already paid for!! If I wasn’t getting screwed out of the subscription that I already paid for, I would have given this 5 stars. Developers, please fix this issue and give me my Pro subscription back!!
author: LRC68

title: Very Pleasant App
body:
This app was very carefully designed and built. The options to customize the colors and sounds help to make it a personal experience. 

There are many Pomodoro apps to choose from, but this one is the most intuitive I’ve used and it helps me to focus - which is what it is all about.
author: Rouviere Media

title: Great for engineering and med students
body: The pomodoro method is a great studying tool to prevent procrastination and to keep yourself from zoning out. This app makes use of this and allows you to absorb information like a sponge while using this method! I highly recommend paying the 2 dollar upgrade, so that you can see your weekly stats and keep your studying streak going!
author: 012Bill

title: Helpful but I really don’t like the red
body: I like the alarm a lot and it’s helpful how easy it is to set up a task. I know this may sound trivial, but the red color all over the screen is really stressful and I find myself avoiding looking at it and feeling immediately more tense when I see it. I wish I could make it blue or something more calming. It’s affected my experience a lot
author: Nikkitysplit9

title: Update made things worse
body: Idk why I can’t switch between 25/5 and 50/10 timers without paying for pro. Paywall on a timer app is annoying. :(
author: afkrgdej

title: Feature Request: Time Elapsed Stopwatch with Timer
body: Great app! It makes me track my productivity progress which is very motivating. But during the timer, I really would like to see time elapse along with countdown timer too.
author: passavudhs

title: Great in theory but app is unreliable
body:
I have used this app for 1 week and have a paid membership.

The app frequently freezes, randomly stops the timer, and sends notifications at incorrect times.

It’s a shame because it’s the best designed pomodoro app by it just isn’t reliable
author: M S 26

title: Basic but broken
body: The app has an annoying handicap that cripple free-to-use version of the app. Scheduled tasks intentionally skips planned days. For such a basic timer / time tracker, there’s no need to pay for a subscription service. Find a free app or write a just write a similar app in a couple hours.
author: waldo1979_

title: Needs Bug Fix
body: Recent update has bug, timer won’t continue if you exit the app or lock your phone screen. Otherwise, previously good app.
author: gbulman96

title: I want a visual mode
body: The pomodoro technique is super powerful and this may be the cleanest app for it, but I really prefer a visualization of my time remaining over the ticking digital clock. A shrinking pie chart gives you the information you actually need—“I have a bit of time left” or “I still have most of my time in this period”—as opposed to the needlessly specific and distracting “I have 12:34 left which is like half of what I started with?”
author: zeitheld

title: Recent releases have problems
body: For a few years now focus keeper has been my favorite Pomodoro timer. Recent releases have had some problems though. Now if I minimize the app it will sometimes pause the timer. And it seems to be in a constant fight with other apps that create audio. For example if I start a podcast and then start the timer it will stop my podcast from playing. Then when I return to start my podcast it pause the timer. It’s been quite frustrating. I hope they can get these problems sorted out soon.
author: Mr first name

title: One feature would make it perfect for me
body: It DOES have the ability to play music, but you can only choose one song. If this could allow you to choose playlists I'd call this a 6 star app.
author: negnom

title: Widget and Siri shortcut support
body: Hope to add widget and Siri shortcut support.
author: j_xnx_

title: Elegant simplicity in my chaotic life!
body:
It’s so hard to cut through all the noise of my week, and I have tried many different productivity tools. FOCUS KEEPER is a gem!

It is just the right number of features without being annoying. It is so easy to use, that there is no “barrier to entry”

Because of its simple elegance, it will integrate well with whatever other system you are using.

USE IT!!
author: working @ Cape Town

title: was good then they updated it
body:
now all the counts are off. was using it for years, now i may have to switch because it doesn’t count accurately. 

some days it shows zero, other days it shows all of that day and the previous day.
author: jeffjlin7

title: Underrated App
body: In this day and age, this app is a must if your hands are glued to your phone. I recently started working with laptop, tablet, and my phone all at the same time and it’s so easy to distract myself. But my job requires technology. So I need something so simple and intuitive to help me focus. I don’t want to spend more time with an app trying to figure out how to work it. You read about self-discipline and watch motivational videos on youtube but they all go to waste if you don’t have the tools to focus on the task you’ve been dying to do! Well, focus keeper. you done did it. Thank you for making my life simple.
author: 8oatmilk8

title: TRACKS YOU—check its "Privacy" link if you disbelieve
body:
These "privacy nutrition labels" do more harm than good, as  Apple does not create or enforce meaningful penalties for deception, as the developer of this app practices. 

Or, is it really okay with Apple (and us consumers, who pay these Apple billionaires and their wealthy shareholders) if a developer checks a couple boxes, like "Does not gather [whatever] data" but omits the truth that using their app will allow you to be tracked by cookies so the developer can sell our info to third parties? 

The big privacy improvements Apple has sold us are merely illusory. We're still being tracked, regardless of the settings we choose or our attempts to purchase only apps that respect our privacy. I'm finished with Apple—& I've never been a Windows or Chrome person. I'm ready just to use a dumb-phone and solely a Linux distro on my machine. Screw it.

title: Doesn’t keep up to date on sessions!
body: My current day and yesterday aren’t shown on the past 14 days. I even paid for this app, which I almost never do. We need to see a ACCURATE RECORD of our sessions each day, else it’s not at all motivating. Very disappointed and will look for other apps.
author: Ivivjvivuvucycjdgdichcn

title: Great app, needs some work
body:
This is a great app and I love how they added the option to create and name multiple tasks, however you must have the same times for each task. 

It would be much better to have the option of saving different times for each task.
author: mellomike840

title: Best and most flexible Pomodoro app
body: I’ve tried them all. Keep coming back to this one, which I use practically every work day. The specific feature that sets this apart from all the rest us the ability to simply dial back or dial forward a few minutes right from the main timer screen.
author: mromanas

title: First year grad student.
body:
This app is helping me get through the long nights of writing and studying for grad school. The long break is a huge incentive that pushes me to get through each focus session. It’s such a simple concept that truly helps you stay focused.

UPDATE: I use this app religiously, but it has not been working the same for me recently. The timer stops whenever I lock the screen or when I go to a different app. So I’ll be working, waiting for the timer to go off. Then when I check it again, the timer is at the same time from when I locked my screen, and it is unpaused. Please fix this. I rely on this app far too much.
author: geezluisa

title: Great app!
body: I use daily for my work as a digital court reporter, but would love to be able to free my phone and use this on my Apple Watch. I’m looking forward to a future Apple Watch app!!
author: Heydarcy

title: Works until it doesn’t
body: It’ll work great for a bit and then it’ll do things like put you on a random date on the calendar or have the timer go extremely slow or pause the timer when you leave the app or not count rounds. To test this, I set a timer on my watch at the exact time my 25 minute timer started in this app and when my watch went off the app said I had 18 more minutes. It’ll work until it doesn’t. Then you have delete and reinstall it. Not worth it.
author: megan11607

title: New update
body: Not a fan of this new update. It was simple and intuitive before. Newest edition has what seems like unnecessary new features that are kind of confusing.
author: MDH7075

title: I loved the 1.0 version. The new version is somehow disappointing
body:
I really love this app because it helps with organizing my time so well.

But there’re couple of bugs I’ve noticed recently. As many users have mentioned, the timer just stopped counting when running in the background. Also, sometimes it over counts —— how am I able to work for 40 hours per day? But this is what I was told... Hopefully, developers will get them fixed soon
author: 学号6720774

title: Great but ‘charting’ function is elusive
body: Lovely simple pomodoro style app. Only caveat: The ‘charting’ page - graph that tracks your focus sessions over time doesn’t register anything- for me anyways. The ‘help’ link just leads to an explanation on data privacy -so no quick way to assess if this user error.
author: tlas1312

title: It is great idea, but needs lots of improvements
body:
Generally it is a good idea, but there plenty of things that need to be rethought. Have you actually tested it with users before creating the app? 
Pomidoro is a great system, but this app makes it very inflexible. For instance you can change a quick break to long break, and even if you skip you can’t get there. There are few more important aspects such as setting different timers for different activities that is not addressed.
author: Orderxaos

title: ABSOLUTELY NOT
body: was using this app for TWO YEARS and then it automatically updated and lost ALLLLLLL my data. Contacted customer support repeatedly to try to recover data, but seems like they e given up. Do NOT buy! Let us revert to old version!!
author: Oxidizing nfyxt

title: Used to be a big fan but recent updates have made this clunky
body: I used this app religiously for school and loved it. I feel the recent updates have added too many features and the interface is not as intuitive as it used to be. Additionally I am regularly seeing the timer pause without me pressing anything.
author: SewaneeRights

title: Please support watchOS
body: It’s not so convenient to use focus keeper without iPhone.Please consider transferring it to watchOS.
author: Lineal Micheal

title: This app is great, but…
body:
The Pomodoro Technique has been vital in order for me to stay on task, and making sure that the most reliable Pomo app with do the work… 

I love this app, but I’m giving this three stars because having your phone closed frequently stops/freezes the timer, which leads to never knowing if you’ve finished a task on time, or how much time was left. Will be deleting unfortunately because of this.
author: Jonni Thunder

title: Great product BUT…
body: I’ve been using this as my go to focus keeper. BUT why is the limit to focus sessions 60 minutes??? I like to go long so would love to see the max minutes of focus at 120 or at leas 90. Seems like an easy fix. How about  it?
author: oemnot

title: What happened?
body:
This is an app that definitely had four stars and now it has one.The reason why is because there was a change a couple of updates ago in the app does not run as smoothly as it used to. I used to be able to look at the internet and read a book on my phone while the timer was running. I can no longer do that. In fact, when the timer stops it would stop the audio from the book I was reading or the video I was watching online. I did not want that.

That start, however now if I’m on the Internet listening to a song watching something the timer stops. Earlier today I was on a phone call and I set my timer for 25 minutes and 45 minutes later it still Hatten wrong because the timer stopped when I excepted the phone call! That is an acceptable! 

Originally this was a four star review because I made a change shortly after I got it and no longer had access to the soothing sounds during my lunch break. This went from a four star to a one star review because  they didn’t fix the issues. II took the app off my phone because I couldn’t leave a review! But now I’m going to remove it from my phone again because there has to be something better out there!
author: JayCee DeeCee

title: Generally good app, but more analytics to make pro worth it
body: I’m happy with how the app functions, and I like the ability to work on separate tasks with different colors. But I would like to see that time broken up by color in the charts. Otherwise, what’s the point of the colored tasks? I can’t see how much time I’ve spent on a particular task at the end of the week or month. Will update my review to 5 stars if this feature becomes available :)
author: Fishero0

title: Horrendous Update
body: Used to think this app was amazing! However, since the newest update they’ve been asking me to pay for things I’d been using in the past for free. Wouldn’t be that big of an issue but the bugs are here as well. Please go back…
author: N3chos13

title: Recent updates have ruined a great app
body: The simple fact is the last couple updates have broken what used to be a bullet proof app. I don’t want tasks. I want a timer that keeps track of segments flawlessly, and this app no longer does this. I’m tired of coming back to the app and finding it’s skipped ten segments ahead for no reason. I’ll be looking for something new that’s focused on being a great timer above and beyond any other gimmicks.
author: dbvoegtle

title: Frustrating Bugs
body: I adore this app for the most part, but I’ve had issues with it pausing timers (focus and break) randomly when I’m either on another screen or even if my screen just goes dark on the app. It also doesn’t properly calculate my time spent over 14 days like it’s supposed to. Despite using it for hours almost every day, it says I’ve used 0 minutes or 0 rounds, even though specific days keep accurate track. It’s minor, but it would greatly help me keep track of how often I study over a period of time.
author: Bradlee V

title: Helps me stay on task
body: Love this app! It makes it easy to keep track of my productivity and keeps me focused.
author: Jennxxd

title: Big step back with v2.0
body: I was an enthusiastic user of the previous version - it was simple, clean, customizable, and let me keep track at a basic level of actual time spent on key projects. The “improved” version is fiddly and unnecessarily complex - but far worse than that, the record-keeping function is just broken. For example, I completed six focus sessions yesterday and the bar chart inexplicably credits me with 18. I’ve switched to a competing product.
author: Matt Ashbury

title: Task feature would be useful if fixed
body: I like to segment my day to make sure I put time towards work projects and personal recharge time … right now, if i create daily tasks for all of those segments, the counters work independently (per task) and sessions don’t *collectively* count towards my daily goal. this needs to be fixed. if my goal is 20 sessions, then i should be able to spent 4 sessions in task A, then 6 sessions on task B, and so on. and then i should see that time spent on those separate tasks collectively count towards my daily goal.
author: i.togusa

title: Major bug in newest update
body: I have used Focus Keeper for years. There is a major bug in the newest update where the timer pauses when you turn off your phone or do something else on your phone with the app in the background. Then when you turn your phone back on or open the app the timer starts ticking again like nothing happened.
author: Malcolm Wolf

title: Great app but having one issue
body: I have been confused why it seems like I have been working for many hours a day when the app shows I have only worked for maybe 5. Today I started working at 8:30am and was working non-stop except for short breaks. My app was set to work for 52 minutes and take an 8 minute break each hour. I just checked 5 hours later and it shows I’ve only worked for just over an hour. I don’t know what, if anything, I am doing wrong. It’s not that complicated of an app.
author: ZOINKSscoobhehe

title: Used to be great
body: This app used to be wonderful but the latest update broke the timer counter and the new features aren’t useful to me since the timer goals aren’t broken up between tasks. I’m sad I have to find another app
author: Qyler

title: Awesome app, but most features require subscription
body:
This is an absolutely fantastic app for structuring your time trying to be productive. I use it almost every day for work.

I believe I paid less than $10 to unlock all the features back when this was a one-time purchase. Now it is a $6/year subscription. Yes, it’s very cheap, but I wish they had just kept it as a one-time purchase for newcomers. Thankfully I’m grandfathered into the Pro version with my initial purchase. I just had to go to the app settings and select “restore pro” to get all my features back. 

I can’t comment on the “tasks” part of the app since it seems pretty basic and unnecessary. Personally, I already use Todoist (another excellent productivity app) for task management.
author: Self-promoting

title: New version is terrible
body:
There is no option for silence during a focus session, and then seamlessly switching to ticking or rain or whatever during breaks. I used to enjoy hearing the difference between break and work. Now, if I have it muted,  because I don’t want sound while I’m working, I will miss the sound that alerts me to break time. 

I’ve never been able to use the music feature, but even now, I can’t even switch to “music” and let it be silent. 

The task list makes no sense and doesn’t help. 

Instead of seeing how many minutes are left in a session from the Home Screen on my iPad (it used to show minutes left in the corner of the icon just like any app with alerts), it shows how many tasks I have left, or just nothing if I don’t have tasks and am only using the timer. 

Moving to a task-based system for a timer is just weird. 

Focus keeper app is now absolutely useless. I cannot use it like this. Please revert back. This is one of the few apps I’ve ever paid for the full version of because I really liked it and used it all the time. Now I can’t use it at all. The new changes have totally eliminated every useful feature the app had. I don’t know how to further stress the point that the new changes have made the app unusable, as in, any feature a person would want from a pomodoro timer app is no longer included in the app.
author: Bex n effex

title: I want the old application back!
body: The new design is incredibly annoying and doesn’t allow for the tracking of multiple sessions. The To-Do list isn’t useful. Please revert back!
author: jjkbb2005

title: New update is horrible
body: Keeps messing up count of pomodoros and no longer tracks 2-week average correctly. Sad because I used the old version for years, but now I’ll be switching.
author: jeanjiwooyi07

title: Don’t overcomplicate things.
body: I originally purchased this app because I wanted a simple, nice-looking pomodoro timer. Now, it’s a cluttered mess with todo lists and a million settings.
author: Chicagoat

title: The app resets time :(
body: I love the layout and how easy the app is to use. Suddenly they switched to a subscription model and I am downgraded to a “free” user. They literally STOLE my money and removed features previously available overnight. 

Is this how you treat loyal paying costumers?

title: Solid, but with a couple key flaws
body:
While this version of the app has more features than the previous, I have two main complaints. The first is that the app icon’s badge no longer reflects how much time you have left in a session. I relied on this to quickly command-tab while writing and see how much time I had left without overly interrupting my work flow. Now I must go all the way into the app to find this information, which is more disruptive.

Second, and more fatally, this is now a subscription app. While I understand that developers would like to have a steady income, not every little app (such as a timer) warrants constant payments. I appreciate that the developers may feel that the added functionality warrants this, but for what I want, which is a simple pomodor-style timer, the cost is just too much. Think I’ll stick with the one-time $2 payment “pro” version and hope that keeps working.

title: NEW UPDATE RUINED IT
body:
I use to love the previous version of Focus Keeper. It was simple and effective, I was able to pause the time and exit the app and still have my study time saved for the day so I could pick up where I had left off. I would’ve given this a 5/5 if it weren’t for the new version. The new version seems more complicated and just unnecessary, the features are the same but there are many times when I have to pause my timer, for example at the time 12/25 minutes, and exit the app. Then, I suddenly lose my study hours and it goes back to beginning with 25 minutes. This used to not happen with the previous version at all! This is extremely frustrating for me because there are times when I really have to pause the timer and go to another app, but when I come back to the app I’d expect to pick up to where I left off. 
Really hope they improve this version or set it back to the previous version, because the previous version was very simple and effective, with no lags at all.

title: ADHD life saver
body:
Are your projects ever so big you don’t know where to start? Or do you struggle to see the trees from the forest when you get too interested in something? I admit this is the first app of time cycling I have tried so I don’t  have experience with competitors but this app has been a lifesaver. Making sure I have planned breaks helps me stop going even if I really want to continue. This avoids me wasting time when I get lost in the trees and not seeing the forest. The 5 min breaks are also nice. They save me from taking a break to do something and never getting back on task because one thing leads to another. 

Thanks for developing a tool that is so simple but at the same time so valuable. This gives me structure in a sea of unending curiosity and saves me from just jumping from one thing to the next.

I agree with others that in a further iteration of the app it would be wonderful to label focus sessions. Linking to a calendar or even a graph to get visual representation of time spent would also be an awesome features.

title: I use it everyday
body:
This time is so simple and elegant. The timer just works and the interface is clutter free. I appreciate that there is a calculator that shows how much time you would be spending in Focus when setting up the rounds, which I find helps me stay realistic with my focus goals. I do about 8 rounds in a work day, which is about 4.5 hours of focus, and usually takes a whole work day. With this feature I can let myself off the hook for not working enough because I am not working “16 hours a day” as so many people in my field like to trumpet. When I can complete my work ahead of schedule with a regular rhythm of focus, all the workaholic unrealistic expectations start to dissolve

One feature that’s keeping this from being a five star review is that there is no option to have a sustained alarm to alert the end of a long break. When it’s the end of a long break usually I am away from my phone far enough that the one time ding doesn’t register to me until it’s too late and I need to reset the focus timer.

title: Helping me through my roughest day

This app is a lifesaver for my ADHD brain. I turned on the White Noise app and set the timer for 10 minutes. So far I’ve been able to complete 3 cycles of 10 minutes each. I’ve now bumped it up to 15 minutes. Hopefully the apps will carry me through the day.

Update 10/6 - I have one complaint about the way the app functions. I have it installed on my iPhone. It seems to stop randomly and it doesn’t restart itself or even alert me to let me know that I need to restart it. I don’t know if it stops when I get a text message or a phone call or if a calendar alert pops up. I’m so focused on my work (or trying to be focused re:ADHD). I only realize that the timer has stopped when I switch to it to see how much time is left until my next break. It’s very frustrating.

title: Completely Changes the WFH Balance
body:
After switching from 5-6 days a week in the office, to COVID and working from home, I really struggled to balance everything. Somehow the load of laundry or the dishes in the sink were very hard to ignore while trying to focus on work. I found myself constantly distracted, only able to focus on work when household tasks were done (which of course they never are!)
This app changed my life. The structure of working for 25 minutes with a 5 minute break allows for focus time, and then I can take 5 minutes to switch the laundry or empty the dishwasher, which really helps to keep the work-life balance actually balanced. Four repeats of a “block” equals 8 hours of focus, which also makes a very tangible way to work 8 hours during your day. And this is broken up by 30 minute breaks between each two hour block, which I find helps me produce higher quality work throughout the day, while also giving me time to keep up with housework. 
I highly recommend focus keeper to anyone struggling to work from home and keep their work life balance.

But this app has been extremely helpful in reminding me to take breaks, and then use my super power of hyperfocus to get things done. I definitely recommend this to a lot of people who are struggling with distractions, and one thing that I would change, is being able to set a title during each focus session so that I know exactly what I should be focusing on. I use stickies at the moment and then crumble them when I’m done (which is so rewarding). Definitely will be using this... without I think I would be homeless because I wouldn’t get any work done. title: Great app, but...
body:
So I’ve only been using this for a few days to help keep my focus on work at home instead of all the background activity that I don’t usually have when I was working in the office. 

Generally speaking, I really do like this and find it easier to keep my focus on my tasks knowing I’ve got a short break coming up. I like the functionality of the app - I appreciate the simplicity and ease in using it. 

My only complaint is that, if I have to switch apps, it will stop the clock. I know the point is to focus, but my employer is using a VOIP app to let us answer our calls via our mobile phones while at home, meaning I don’t really have a choice about switching between this and the phone app. But, when I switch back, the timer has often stopped. And, if I forget to switch back and check it, then I’m often sitting there thinking to myself that it seems like a really long 25 minutes! If this bug was fixed, I would absolutely give this app 5 stars.

title: My favorite Pomodoro timer
body:
Of the many Pomodoro technique timers I’ve downloaded on my phone and desktop to help me stay focused during my work sprints, this has by far been my favorite. I’m a stickler for good, intuitive UX, especially when it comes to productivity apps. The last thing I need when trying to get work done is an app that takes too long to customize or setup! I love that I can readjust my focus segments right there on the timer page with a simple slider, rather than being forced into the options to make a universal change. That way, my focus segments can fit any sort of scheduling fluctuations or preferences that day. Signals and alarms when the segments are up are loud enough over any background focus music I’m using, but aren’t jarring.

Overall, I highly recommend this app for anyone needing help to focus and get work done with a simple setup!

title: Nuther ADHD/ND approved
body:
I knew this technique existed, but this app made it so easy to implement. There are three different phases to this timer, and five “rounds”: two 25-min work rounds, two 5-min break rounds, and one 25-min break round. Each different phase has a different sound to it, so it’s easy to know which round is happening without having to pick up your phone and reset. This is a HUGE bonus for me, since picking up my phone is focus suicide. You can leave this open, even with your phone on silent, and still hear the time ticking away, which is enough auditory stimulation for me to focus on what I’m doing. It will go through the phases without you having to touch anything. This is all for free, by the way. Additional customization options are available for a one-time purchase, but the app can stand on its own without these. Perfect!

I use this on my iPhone 7 for refs sake

I have literally been more productive in my very first time of using this app, that I have in MONTHS! This is my new life saver and I would totally recommend this to ANYONE with ADD/ ADHD. I feel more accomplished and at ease because I am getting my work caught up in long sittings!!! The routine breaks are perfect!!! title: Helpful for ADD
body:
I have never written a review before. However, this app has changed my life. I have ADD. When I tried to study before I  used this app, I had to spend an unsustainable amount of time to complete my work. This was because I was constantly getting distracted. Now, when I work, I always have my cell phone out on my desk with this app going. For me, distraction always starts with me looking up and around. Now, when I do that, I see this app’s “focus session” screen counting away. Then I remember that I am on “focus” time, and get back to my task. Also, knowing I have a guilt-free break coming up makes me not rebel against focusing for 25 minutes. The knowledge that I will have time to get important things done besides studying motivates me. 

I recommend getting the pro version. Being able to adjust the time for breaks is essential for me. I am a mother, so the things that I used to try to multitask, I now do one at a time during my breaks. Sometimes, I need more than 5 minutes to finish the dishes, etc. I can adjust the time of each break on the “break screen” with pro. It takes 2 seconds. Setting my chores, studying, etc up this way takes away the excuse that I had about needing to do chores or other important things instead of studying. 

Because this app prevents the screen from locking, it never disappears like the regular timer app on my phone. I don’t have to reset it each time a session ends either. It is all automatic. Resetting a timer over and over on my own would never have worked with my ADD. I don’t think I conveyed how much this app has changed my life. It is a night and day difference.

I try to avoid any interaction with my phone when I am working (and therefore using this app) and naturally I use my breaks differently when I have a long break compared to a short break. At the moment, I have to check the timer to see if I have a short or long break but it would be much more preferable to avoid having the pull my phone out as that reintroduces the distractor.

title: Must have for university students.
body:
I love this app. I use it every day for school work. I’ll keep it open on my phone so anytime I start to get distracted and pick up my phone, the bright red screen and timer pops up to remind me I’m on the clock. 

It makes dreadful tasks less dreadful because there is always an end in sight. It makes me feel productive because I can visibly see how much I’ve gotten done. 

I really like to spend the work period working, and the break period cleaning or doing chores. It’s a good way to be active in between long periods of sitting, keeps me awake, and is a nice way to get chores done in short periods that would have otherwise been spent scrolling on my phone. The pomodoro timer is an excellent way to put some much needed routine into my study sessions.

title: Great for Procrastinators
body: This app is a great resource to use to successfully space out your time. One thing I learned about me and other procrastinators is that we often over calculate how much time we need for breaks from productivity. Constant excuses keep people from staying on task, and that’s how time loss happens. This app has really helped me to stay focused because you always know there will be a break after a certain period of work, while also not overdoing it. I like to go with the 25:5 ratio, but you can adjust your times according to your needs. This has helped me keep it a habit to be productive with my time, and it’s really easy to use. Definitely suggest you try it out for a few days and see how it goes! (Because it’s really helpful!)

title: Great Pomodoro for Focus
body:
This app is among best of its kind. I have used pomodoro method for many years, and offered it as a wonderful focus technique as a trainer for my time management courses. Key for me is the ticking sound as a gentle reminder, when I get sidetracked, that I’m “on the clock” with one area of focus. Also, a loud enough beginning and ending alarm is important to make sure I start and or take a break at designated timeframes. 

This app key things fairly simple, which the method is designed to be, yet offers a useful level of automation to make it great.
